summary: Henry Herbert Dodwell (1879–1946) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Lord Williams's School and St John's College (~1898–1902). He served in the Indian Educational Service (1908–1922) and was Professor of History of India at SOAS (~1922–1946).

Henry Pitts Forster (1766–1815) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served in the Bengal Civil Service (~1783–1815) and held the post of Master of the Calcutta Mint at the India Government Mint, Kolkata (~1803–1815).
Henry Sullivan Jarrett (1839–1919) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Succeeding Heinrich Blochmann, he served as Secretary and Member of the Board of Examiners in Calcutta (~1870–1892).

Henry Thomas Colebrooke (1765–1837) was an Indologist who studied under Citrapati. He served in the Bengal Civil Service, Sadar Diwani Adalat, Supreme Council of Bengal, Fort William College (1782–1814), and as director of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1837).

Herbert Franke (1914–2011) specialized in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Cologne, Bonn, and Humboldt University under Erich Haenisch. He served as President of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1980–1985) and taught at Munich.

Herbert Härtel (1921–2005) was an Indologist, historian/archaeologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ernst Waldschmidt (~1948–1953). He served as Director of the Museum für Asiatische Kunst (~1963–1986) and Professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (attested 1993–1994).

Herbert Niel Randle (1880–1973) worked in the fields of Indology and philosophy. He served as Librarian at the India Office (~1927–1949), an affiliation also attested in 1973 at the India Office Library.

Herbert V. Guenther (1917–2006) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan and under several traditional teachers, including Damcho Rinchen and Geshe Ngawang Nyima, later serving as Professor at the University of Saskatchewan (~1964–1984).

Herbert Weir Smyth (1857–1937) was a linguist who studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen. He held academic posts at Williams College (~1881–1882), Johns Hopkins (~1883–1885), Bryn Mawr (~1888–1901), and Harvard University (~1901–1925).

Herman Kellgren (1822–1856) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1844–1846), Eugène Burnouf (~1846–1848), and Philippe-Édouard Foucaux (~1846–1848). He held a post at the University of Helsinki (~1849–1856).
Hermann Beckh (1875–1937) worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1903–1907) and later held an academic post there (~1908–1921).
Hermann Beythan (1875–1945) was a scholar in the fields of Indology and linguistics. He pursued his studies under the traditional teachers Ramasami Aiyar and Radscha Pillai.

Hermann Brockhaus (1806–1877) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Leipzig and under August Wilhelm Schlegel (~1827–1829). He served as Professor Extraordinarius at Jena (1839) and Professor at Leipzig University (1848; 1872–1877).

Hermann Brunnhofer (1841–1916) worked in Indology and studied under Albrecht Weber (~1865–1868). He taught at Goldingen Gymnasium (~1875–1881) and later served as Titularprofessor at the University of Bern (1901–1914).
Hermann Camillo Kellner (1839–1916) worked in the field of Indology. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1861–1865) and served as Gymnasialprofessor at the Gymnasium zu Zwickau (~1868–1904).

Hermann Collitz (1855–1935) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Johanneum Lüneburg and under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen (~1875–1878). He held professorships at Bryn Mawr College (1885–1907) and Johns Hopkins University (1907).

Hermann Goetz (1898–1976) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1920–1923), served as Curator of the Baroda Museum and Picture Gallery (~1939–1953), and held a post at Heidelberg University (~1961–1976).

Hermann Grassmann (1809–1877) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Marienstiftsgymnasium Stettin and Frederick William University Berlin (1827–1830). He held teaching posts at Gewerbeschule, Friedrich-Wilhelms-Gymnasium, and Marienstiftsgymnasium Stettin (1832–1834; 1852–1877).

Hermann Hirt (1865–1936) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Freiburg (~1885–1887) and Leipzig University (~1887–1889), and held posts at Leipzig University (~1896–1912) and the University of Giessen (~1912–1935).

Hermann Jacobi (1850–1937) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Bonn, Humboldt University, and Calcutta. He held posts at the universities of Münster (~1876–1885), Kiel (~1885–1889), Cologne, Munich, and Bonn (attested 1925).
